req.title: Session cookie has HttpOnly attribute
req.statement: The system shall set HttpOnly on the session cookie.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that the session cookie carries the HttpOnly attribute. Flask sets the session cookie on any response that modifies the session (e.g. a successful login). We test: (1) positive – after a valid login the Set-Cookie header contains 'HttpOnly'; (2) negative – a plain GET to a public page that never touches the session should not emit a Set-Cookie header at all, confirming the attribute is tied to session creation; (3) boundary – the HttpOnly flag must be present regardless of which valid user triggers the session, and the cookie name must be the Flask default 'session', catching mutations that strip the flag or rename the cookie. Each test uses an in-process test client, exact string assertions, and checks both presence and absence to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_session_cookie_has_httponly_after_login
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database is initialised with init_db so user 'Rahul'/'stone' exists
expected: HTTP 302 redirect (successful login)
Set-Cookie header is present
Cookie name is 'session'
HttpOnly attribute is present in the Set-Cookie value (case-insensitive)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: session cookie shall have HttpOnly attribute
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_session_cookie_has_httponly_after_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Set-Cookie header must be present after login'
    assert 'session' in set_cookie, 'Cookie name must be session'
    assert 'HttpOnly' in set_cookie, 'HttpOnly attribute must appear in Set-Cookie'

test_session_cookie_has_httponly_after_login()

tests.name: test_httponly_present_for_second_distinct_user_login
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database is initialised; user 'Anjali'/'cloud' exists (user id=2)
actions: Inspect Set-Cookie header for HttpOnly and Secure absence (HTTP context)
expected: HTTP 302 redirect
Set-Cookie header contains 'HttpOnly' exactly once
Cookie attribute string contains 'HttpOnly' (case-sensitive as Flask emits it)
Cookie name 'session' is present
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly must be set for every user session, not just the first
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_httponly_present_for_second_distinct_user_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Set-Cookie header must be present after Anjali login'
    assert 'session' in set_cookie, 'Cookie name must be session'
    assert set_cookie.count('HttpOnly') == 1, (
        f'HttpOnly must appear exactly once, got: {set_cookie}'
    )
    lower = set_cookie.lower()
    assert 'httponly' in lower, 'HttpOnly must be present (case-insensitive check)'

tests.name: test_failed_login_does_not_set_httponly_cookie
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database initialised; wrong password used so login fails
actions: Inspect response status and Set-Cookie header
expected: HTTP 200 (login page re-rendered, not redirected)
No Set-Cookie header with a session value is emitted
Confirms HttpOnly cookie is only set on successful authentication
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly session cookie must only be issued on successful login (state transition boundary)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_failed_login_does_not_set_httponly_cookie():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'wrongpassword'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    if set_cookie:
        assert 'session' not in set_cookie or 'HttpOnly' not in set_cookie, (
            'A session cookie with HttpOnly must NOT be set on failed login'
        )

test_failed_login_does_not_set_httponly_cookie()

tests.name: test_httponly_present_after_logout_redirect_chain
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
actions: POST /auth/login with username=Diya, password=cloud to establish session
Inspect Set-Cookie on the second login response
expected: Second login returns HTTP 302
Set-Cookie header on second login contains 'HttpOnly'
Confirms HttpOnly is set on re-authentication after logout (state transition)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly must be set on every new session, including after logout+re-login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_httponly_present_after_logout_redirect_chain():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r1 = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Diya', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    client.get('/auth/logout')
    r2 = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Diya', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r2.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Set-Cookie must be present on re-login'
    assert 'HttpOnly' in set_cookie, (
        f'HttpOnly must be present after re-login, got: {set_cookie}'
    )
    assert 'session' in set_cookie

test_httponly_present_after_logout_redirect_chain()
